In the low-spin fit with C/B = 4.5, Dq ≈ 1593 cm⁻¹ and B ≈ 778 cm⁻¹, so C ≈ 3500 cm⁻¹ and Δ = 10Dq ≈ 15 930 cm⁻¹.

I used the Tanabe–Sugano fitting tool for d⁶ pinned to the low-spin regime. The tool only accepts a fixed C, so I could not enter C/B = 4.5 directly. I fitted at three trial values of C and picked the one whose fitted B gave C/B = 4.5.

| Fixed C (cm⁻¹) | Fitted Dq (cm⁻¹) | Fitted B (cm⁻¹) | C/B |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2250 | 1527 | 754 | 3.0 |
| 3000 | 1566 | 770 | 3.9 |
| 3500 | 1593 | 778 | 4.50 |

The C = 3500 cm⁻¹ fit is self-consistent with C/B = 4.5. The fit assigns the three observed bands as follows:

| Observed (cm⁻¹) | Assignment | Calculated (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|
| 13 960 | ¹A₁g → ¹T₁g | 13 957 |
| 22 740 | ¹A₁g → ¹T₂g | 22 740 |
| 29 700 | ¹A₁g → ¹T₂g(b) | 29 751 |

The third band is also close to a ¹E_g level at 29 701 cm⁻¹, but the tool lists only the ¹T₂g(b) assignment as allowed. The residuals are about 3 cm⁻¹ or less.
